summary.text: Tiangong, officially the China Space Station, is China's first permanently crewed space station, in low Earth orbit since 2021 and operated by the China Manned Space Agency.
It is a space laboratory hosting experiments on bioastronautics, microgravity, materials science and space technology.
Crews of three travel aboard Shenzhou spacecraft for missions of about six months, while cargo missions use Tianzhou spacecraft.

facts.label: Modules
facts.value: Tianhe core module, then Wentian and Mengtian in 2022

facts.label: Volume
facts.value: 340 cubic metres, slightly over one third of the ISS

facts.label: Rice
facts.value: First full agricultural cycle in microgravity, 2022

items.prompt: China asked to join the ISS program in 2007, and Roscosmos and ESA supported it. Why did China not take part?

options.label: Roscosmos and ESA later refused the request
A US law, the Wolf Amendment, prohibited Chinese participation
The ISS had no room for new partners
China's own station was already finished

items.explain: Roscosmos and ESA supported cooperation, but the Wolf Amendment, enacted by the United States since 2011, prohibited Chinese participation.

items.prompt: Tiangong-1 in 2011 gave China rendezvous and docking experience. What did its successor add in 2016?

options.label: Longer-term life support and autonomous docking and refueling
Rendezvous and docking for the first time
The Wentian laboratory module
A telescope that docks for servicing

items.explain: In 2016, Tiangong-2 developed longer-term life support systems and autonomous docking and refueling via Tianzhou.

items.prompt: Tiangong is built from separately launched modules. Which two modular stations came before it?

options.label: Salyut 1 and Skylab
Mir and Skylab
Mir and the ISS
The ISS and Tiangong-1

items.explain: Tiangong is the third modular space station, after Mir and the ISS.

items.prompt: What is new about how Tiangong holds its position in orbit?

options.label: It uses no thrusters and so drifts freely in space
It relies on docked Soyuz craft to push it along
It borrows thrust from the Tianlian satellite network
It is the first crewed craft to use ion thrusters to hold station

items.explain: Tiangong is the first crewed spacecraft to use ion thrusters for orbital station-keeping.

items.prompt: Why did the crew cultivate rice and the plant Arabidopsis thaliana on the station?

options.label: To explore sustainable food sources for long spaceflights
To test whether plants can create gravity
To feed the animals aboard the Tianzhou ships
To check which plants survive in a vacuum

items.explain: Agriculture in microgravity was explored with rice and Arabidopsis as sustainable food sources for long-term spaceflight.

items.prompt: Crews on Tiangong are normally three people. When do six people live aboard?

options.label: While Tianzhou cargo ships are docked
During handovers between crews
During spacewalks
Whenever a telescope docks for servicing

items.explain: Crews of three travel aboard Shenzhou, with temporary crew sizes of six during handovers.
